segments.ACT.25.1-3: Jewish leaders ask Festus to bring Paul to Jerusalem
segments.ACT.25.4-5: Festus tells the Jewish leaders to accuse Paul in Caesarea
segments.ACT.25.6-8: Paul says he has done nothing wrong before Festus
segments.ACT.25.9-9: Festus asks Paul if he will go to Jerusalem for trial
segments.ACT.25.10-10: Paul says Caesar’s court is the right place for his trial
segments.ACT.25.11-12: Paul appeals to Caesar, and Festus agrees to send him
segments.ACT.25.13-16: Festus tells King Agrippa about Paul’s case
segments.ACT.25.17-20: Festus says the accusers argued about religion and Jesus
segments.ACT.25.21-22: Festus says Paul appealed to Caesar; Agrippa wants to listen
segments.ACT.25.23-24: Festus presents Paul to Agrippa and the leading men
segments.ACT.25.25-27: Festus says Paul did nothing worthy of death
segments.ACT.26.1-3: Paul begins his defense before King Agrippa
segments.ACT.26.4-5: Paul says the Jews know he lived as a Pharisee
segments.ACT.26.6-8: Paul says he is on trial for his hope in God’s promise
segments.ACT.26.9-11: Paul tells how he once harmed the believers in Jesus
segments.ACT.26.12-14: Paul sees a bright light on the road to Damascus
segments.ACT.26.15-18: Jesus appoints Paul to be his servant and witness
segments.ACT.26.19-21: Paul obeys the vision and tells all to turn to God
segments.ACT.26.22-23: Paul says he teaches what Moses and the prophets said
segments.ACT.26.24-26: Festus says Paul is insane, but Paul speaks words of truth
segments.ACT.26.27-29: Paul tells Agrippa he wishes all could be like him
segments.ACT.26.30-32: Agrippa and Festus agree Paul has done nothing wrong
segments.ACT.27.1-2: Paul and other prisoners sail for Italy with Julius
segments.ACT.27.3-6: Paul sails past Cyprus and changes ships at Myra
segments.ACT.27.7-8: The ship sails slowly to Fair Havens on Crete
segments.ACT.27.9-11: Paul warns of danger, but the centurion does not listen
segments.ACT.27.12-12: The majority decide to sail on to Phoenix for winter
segments.ACT.27.13-13: The sailors leave when a gentle south wind blows
segments.ACT.27.14-16: A strong wind called the Northeaster drives the ship
segments.ACT.27.17-18: The crew tie the ship with ropes and throw out cargo
segments.ACT.27.19-20: The men lose all hope of being saved from the storm
segments.ACT.27.21-22: Paul tells the men to be brave; only the ship will be lost
segments.ACT.27.23-26: Paul says an angel promised that all on the ship will live
segments.ACT.27.27-29: Sailors sense land near and drop four anchors
segments.ACT.27.30-32: Paul stops the sailors from escaping in the lifeboat
segments.ACT.27.33-35: Paul urges everyone on the ship to eat
segments.ACT.27.36-38: The 276 people on the ship eat and throw out the grain
segments.ACT.27.39-41: The ship runs aground on a sandbar near a beach
segments.ACT.27.42-44: The centurion saves Paul and everyone reaches land safely
segments.ACT.28.1-2: The people of Malta are kind and light a fire
segments.ACT.28.3-4: A snake bites Paul and islanders think he is guilty
segments.ACT.28.5-6: Paul is not hurt, and the islanders say he is a god
segments.ACT.28.7-10: Paul heals Publius’s father and other sick people
segments.ACT.28.11-12: Paul and the others sail from Malta to Syracuse
segments.ACT.28.13-15: Paul reaches Rome, and believers come to meet him
segments.ACT.28.16-18: Paul tells the Jewish leaders in Rome why he is a prisoner
segments.ACT.28.19-20: Paul says he is bound because of the hope of Israel
segments.ACT.28.21-22: The Jewish leaders in Rome want to hear Paul
segments.ACT.28.23-24: Paul teaches many people about Jesus; some believe
segments.ACT.28.25-26: Paul quotes Isaiah as the Jews disagree and leave
segments.ACT.28.27-27: Paul says the people’s hearts have become hard
segments.ACT.28.28-29: Paul says God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles
segments.ACT.28.30-31: Paul stays two years in Rome and preaches boldly
